LibTmux.Version

Description

Parse and order tmux release identities, and check the minimum release.

These functions consume supplied text. They neither execute tmux -V nor contact a server. Admission is a floor: every release at or above 3.3a passes, with no upper bound. Admission says nothing about which releases the project has tested, and individual features still need capability and conformance checks.

Use parseVersion for input, requireSupported for minimum-version admission and renderVersion for the spelling tmux reports.

>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderVersion (parseVersion "tmux 3.3a\n" >>= requireSupported)
Right "3.3a"

Numeric components compare as numbers, and a patch letter follows its release:

>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.9" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
Right True
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10a"
Right True

A development build or release candidate ranks below the release it precedes:

>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "next-3.10" <*> parseVersion "3.10-rc"
Right True
>>> (<) <$> parseVersion "3.10-rc2" <*> parseVersion "3.10"
Right True

Release identity and errors

data TmuxVersion Source #

A tmux release, release candidate or development build, constructed by parseVersion and rendered by renderVersion. Ordering compares the numeric components, then next-X.Y < X.Y-rc < X.Y-rcN < X.Y < X.Ya. Rendering reproduces the accepted spelling, so X.Y-rc and X.Y-rc1 are distinct.

Parse and render

parseVersion :: Text -> Either VersionError TmuxVersion Source #

Parse a release identity or the output of tmux -V, allowing a leading tmux and one final LF. The accepted forms are X.Y, X.Ya, X.Y-rc, X.Y-rcN and next-X.Y. Unknown suffixes, including a bare master, are rejected rather than assigned a guessed release. Diagnostics retain at most 64 chars.

renderVersion :: TmuxVersion -> Text Source #

Render the release as tmux spells it, without the executable name or newline. Parsing the result returns an equal value.

Admit a release

requireSupported :: TmuxVersion -> Either VersionError TmuxVersion Source #

Admit every release at or above 3.3a, including intermediate releases, newer releases and the development builds and candidates ranked above it. Plain 3.3 and older releases fail. The check has no upper bound, so passing it does not mean the project tested that release. Individual features need their own capability checks; passing this check does not qualify an entire release.
